title: Abelian etale sheaves on a field and discrete G-modules
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], $K^{\rm sep}$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field containing $K^{\rm sep}$ over $K$. Put $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/K)$ with its Krull topology and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ be the induced geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Taking the geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] at $\bar s$, with the action induced by changing pointed etale lifts, induces an equivalence between abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and discrete $G$-modules [def-exc-discrete-modules-category] (abelian groups with a $G$-action by group automorphisms and open stabilizers). The equivalence is compatible with the underlying sheaf-of-sets/discrete $G$-set equivalence and with addition, zero, and inverse. Discrete $G$-sets use the discrete continuous-action category as in [lem-exc-etale-field-gsets].

proof.text: By the sheaf-of-sets point equivalence, taking the geometric stalk at Spec Ω identifies sheaves of sets on the small etale site of Spec K with discrete G-sets, where G = Gal(K^sep/K), and the identification is the stalk functor used in the statement.

An abelian sheaf is a sheaf of sets equipped with a commutative group law, and a discrete G-module is a discrete G-set equipped with a commutative group law whose operations are G-equivariant. The product-preserving equivalence therefore transports the addition, zero, and inverse operations and their morphisms, giving an equivalence of the corresponding abelian categories, compatible with the underlying sheaf-of-sets/G-set equivalence and with all abelian group operations.

statement_change.what: Spec K^sep is not a geometric point under the project definition for an imperfect field: for K = F_p(t), the separable closure has no p-th root of t and is not algebraically closed. Use an algebraically closed extension Ω containing K^sep, as in Stacks 04JQ and 03QW; specify the canonical action by extensions of elements of Gal(K^sep/K).
